resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give a 60-foot pole tower; a June 1925 item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page gives 70 feet; WillhiteWeb and the Forest Lookouts page give 76 feet from ground to roof. The story reports the range and does not settle it.
The register text, firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts page and WillhiteWeb all give 1986. The register's photo caption gives 2001. The story uses 1986.

The register and firelookout.com give 1916 for the pole platform. A 1914 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page describes a station recently constructed on First Thought Hill. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Reads: register, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts page (two greps on the cached page), Waymarking lookout page (returned only its title), WillhiteWeb (full page), Waymarking Orient town page (returned no matching text). Two WebSearches: one for the Orient cab, one for park access. The FFA Washington list was reused from the Deming pass. Access 'public' rests on the cab's placement in a community park and the 1985 plan for a historical point of interest; no fetched source gives visiting hours or confirms public entry, and the Waymarking text that mentions the park being open to the public was seen only in a search snippet and is not used. Sibling record flag, not a correction to this one: us-wa-first-thought height_m 21.3 (about 70 feet) fits the 1925 pole tower, not the 40-foot 1947 steel tower the L-4 cab came from. Whoever edits that record should check it. The record for this Orient entry has no height, so none is given here.
